name: MegaManager Connector
author: GDimitrov

sections.description:
MegaManager Connector integrates your WordPress site with the MegaManager platform, allowing you to manage and monitor your site remotely.

Key features include:

  • Real-time monitoring – Monitor your site’s health and availability.
  • Automated backups – Schedule and manage full-site backups stored in the cloud.
  • Remote updates – Update WordPress core, plugins, and themes from the MegaManager dashboard.
  • Cache management – Clear page cache, object cache, and OPcache directly from the admin bar or remotely.
  • Plugin management – Activate or deactivate plugins from the MegaManager interface.
  • Secure communication – All requests are authenticated using HMAC signatures.
  • Database optimization – Analyze and optimize database tables remotely.
  • Maintenance mode – Enable or disable maintenance mode without writing files to the plugin directory.

External Services

This plugin connects to the MegaManager platform API in order to provide remote site management features.

API endpoint used by the plugin:

https://ytpejlwklmtsdletzqvv.supabase.co/functions/v1

What data is sent and when

Site registration (on connect)
When you connect the plugin using a Connect Token, the following information is sent once:

  • Site URL
  • WordPress version
  • PHP version
  • A generated site secret used for request authentication

Heartbeat (every 5 minutes while connected)
To maintain the connection status between your site and MegaManager, the plugin periodically sends:

  • Site ID
  • WordPress version
  • PHP version
  • Site URL

This heartbeat confirms that the site is reachable. It does not include site content, personal data, or analytics information.

Metrics (hourly – optional)
If telemetry is enabled in the plugin settings, performance metrics are sent hourly. These may include:

  • TTFB (Time To First Byte)
  • Page size
  • Installed plugin list
  • Active theme
  • PHP and WordPress versions
  • Disk usage
  • Database size
  • Basic activity logs

Telemetry is disabled by default and requires explicit opt-in in the plugin settings. It can be disabled at any time.

Backup operations

When cloud backups are initiated, database and wp-content files are uploaded to MegaManager storage using temporary signed URLs.

No data is transmitted until the plugin is explicitly connected using a Connect Token from the MegaManager dashboard.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the megamanager-connector folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Settings → MegaManager in the WordPress admin.
  4. Enter your Connect Token from the MegaManager dashboard.
  5. Click Connect to MegaManager.
sections.faq:
How do I connect my site?

After installing the plugin, go to Settings → MegaManager, enter your Connect Token from the MegaManager dashboard, and click Connect.

Is my data secure?

Yes. All communication between your site and MegaManager is authenticated using HMAC-signed requests. The site secret is generated locally and stored on your site.

What caching plugins are supported?

MegaManager Connector supports the following caching plugins:

WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Fastest Cache, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket, Autoptimize, SG Optimizer, Hummingbird, WP-Optimize, and Breeze.

Does this plugin send data without my consent?

No. The plugin only communicates with the MegaManager service after you explicitly connect it using a Connect Token.

Performance metrics are disabled by default and require explicit opt-in via the telemetry setting.
sections.changelog:
1.2.2

  • COMPLIANCE: Removed auto_update_plugin and auto_update_theme filters to comply with WordPress.org plugin review (no modification of core/plugin/theme update behavior)
  • Read-only update checks (wp_update_plugins, wp_update_themes, get_plugin_updates, get_theme_updates, get_core_updates) retained for metrics/reporting only

1.2.1

  • COMPLIANCE: Contributors updated to wpsupporting (WordPress.org username)
  • COMPLIANCE: Maintenance page CSS now uses wp_register_style() and wp_add_inline_style()
  • COMPLIANCE: Backup admin page assets now use wp_enqueue_style() / wp_enqueue_script()
  • COMPLIANCE: Backup temporary directory now uses wp_upload_dir() with plugin-specific subdirectory
  • COMPLIANCE: Removed global FS_METHOD override

1.2.0

  • SECURITY: Removed sslverify=false from outbound requests
  • STABILITY: Fixed is_plugin_active() errors in cron/frontend contexts
  • STABILITY: Limited disk usage scan (max 50,000 files) and media inventory (max 500 images)
  • STABILITY: Added exception handling for filesystem iterators
  • CRON: Improved custom schedule registration
  • COMPLIANCE: Removed legacy auto-login functionality
  • COMPLIANCE: Expanded External Services documentation

1.1.0

  • SECURITY: Removed insecure URL-based auto-login
  • SECURITY: Hardened REST API permission callbacks for PHP 8+
  • COMPLIANCE: Added telemetry opt-in setting
  • COMPLIANCE: Added External Services disclosure
  • COMPLIANCE: Removed direct file writes in wp-content
  • COMPLIANCE: Replaced inline CSS/JS with proper WordPress enqueue usage

1.0.1

  • Added backward-compatible remote backup support

1.0.0

  • Initial release
